name: Next.js
summary: React framework with server rendering, static generation, file-based routing and React Server Components.
use_cases: Full-stack React apps, marketing sites with dynamic sections, SaaS dashboards.
tradeoffs: Caching and rendering modes add conceptual complexity.
Some features are smoothest on Vercel; self-hosting needs more setup for parity.
avoid_if: you want a backend-only API service or a non-React UI.

name: React
summary: UI library for building component-based interfaces; the base for frameworks like Next.js and React Router.
use_cases: Interactive single-page apps, design systems, rich client UIs.
tradeoffs: Not a full framework: routing, data loading and rendering strategy need extra choices.
avoid_if: you want batteries-included routing, data loading and SSR out of the box.

name: React Router (formerly Remix)
summary: React routing library whose framework mode (the successor to Remix v2) adds SSR, loaders and actions.
use_cases: React apps built around web standards and progressive enhancement; migrating Remix apps.
tradeoffs: Branding and API changed during the Remix to React Router v7 merge, so older guides can be misleading.
avoid_if: you want React Server Components as the core rendering model today.

name: SvelteKit
summary: Full-stack framework for Svelte with SSR, static generation, file-based routing and deploy adapters.
use_cases: Fast, small-bundle web apps; teams that prefer a compiler-based UI approach.
tradeoffs: Smaller ecosystem and hiring pool than React.
avoid_if: you depend on React-specific component libraries.

name: FastAPI
summary: Python web framework for building APIs with type hints, async support and automatic OpenAPI docs.
use_cases: Python REST/JSON APIs, ML/AI model serving, backends for SPA or mobile clients.
tradeoffs: API-focused: no built-in ORM, admin UI or templating conventions.
avoid_if: you want a batteries-included framework with ORM and admin panel.

name: Django
summary: Batteries-included Python web framework with ORM, migrations, auth and an admin interface.
use_cases: Content-heavy sites, internal tools, CRUD-heavy products, apps that benefit from a built-in admin.
tradeoffs: Opinionated monolith; async support is improving but not end-to-end everywhere.
avoid_if: you only need a lightweight async API.

name: NestJS
summary: Structured Node.js server framework with dependency injection, modules and decorators.
use_cases: Larger TypeScript backends, microservices, teams that want enforced architecture.
tradeoffs: More boilerplate and abstraction than minimal frameworks.
avoid_if: you are building a small service and want minimal ceremony.

name: Ruby on Rails
summary: Convention-over-configuration Ruby framework with ORM, background jobs and WebSockets (Action Cable).
use_cases: Rapid product development by small teams, CRUD-heavy SaaS, server-rendered apps.
tradeoffs: Ruby-only; smaller talent pool than JavaScript or Python in some markets.
avoid_if: your team works primarily in TypeScript or Python.
